If so, we might be hitting a race where the second token invalidates the first and Coupa is returning the wrong tenant mapping. Rafael, I remember we patched a token rotation last month; could that interact with resend flows?

Next steps: Rafael to pull invite logs + token trace; Marissa to approve manual activation if we confirm it's safe. Neha, flag if this needs an audit record.

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 11:28:45 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: PrimeParts - supplier onboarding invite

I pulled the invite flow traces from our provisioning service and attached a short export (invite_token_trace.log).

Observations:
- We generated two distinct tokens for e.torres@primeparts.com within ~90s (2028-03-09T08:10:54Z and 2028-03-09T08:12:15Z).
- Coupa responded to the second activation with a 200 OK but returned a tenant id that doesn't match the company id in our mapping table (tenant_id 0x7fa2 vs expected 0x5b33). The first token validation returned a 409 conflict during a background tenant bind job.
- It looks like if a resend happens while the background bind completes, the latter token's callback path can race and attach the wrong session to the user — effectively a token swap.

I recommend:
1) Manual activation for PrimeParts on their correct tenant (I can run the bind script safely).
2) Short-term mitigation: prevent immediate re-issuing of a new token for the same email for 5 minutes after the first is sent (rate-limit resend).
3) Longer-term: add idempotency to the tenant bind callback and log a full audit record to avoid silent tenant swaps.

If you approve manual bind, I'll execute and confirm with Elena.

—Rafael

Attachment: invite_token_trace.log (text/plain)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Thanks Rafael — that analysis tracks with what I suspected. Approved: please proceed with manual tenant bind for PrimeParts (company id expected 0x5b33). Rafael, mark the operation in change log CHG-20280310-pp-bind and include the pre/post tenant mapping in the audit.

Neha — please create an audit ticket and retain the invite trace and screenshots under the PrimeParts procurement folder for 6 months. We'll need that for any downstream chargeback / vendor dispute. Also engage Coupa support if we see repeated occurrences for other vendors.

Evelyn — please let Elena know we'll do the manual fix and schedule a short follow-up to confirm activation.

-Marissa

Elena — done. I ran the bind and verified the PrimeParts account now shows the correct company profile and remit code in our test tenant. I also invalidated the outstanding secondary token so it cannot be reused.

Summary of work performed (audit):
- CHG-20280310-pp-bind: manual tenant bind executed by rafael.mendes at 2028-03-11T16:30:22Z
- Pre-bind tenant mapping: tenant_id 0x7fa2 (orphaned session)
- Post-bind tenant mapping: tenant_id 0x5b33 (PrimeParts canonical)
- Invalidated tokens: 2 (timestamps in invite_token_trace.log)

Action items we've raised: COUPA-TICKET-7821 (partner support — request to add idempotent bind callback) and a short-term resend lock to avoid immediate token re-issuance.

Please confirm you can log in and see the company profile. If you still hit the original error, tell us the exact steps and I'll escalate to Coupa.

Best,
Rafael
